# WHY v1.0.52 EXISTS, AND WHY THIS BOM IS SHORT
# v1.0.51 WAS BUILT, INSTALLED BY ANDY ON HARDWARE, AND WALKED. Its record
# (walks/v1.0.51.tsv) is the FIRST in this project's history whose
# artefact_sha256_source is measured(...) rather than asserted -- 82a621e0...,
# shasum of OstlerInstaller-1.0.51.dmg taken on the walked box. verdict FAILED,
# qa_exit 1, pass 12 / fail 4 / cannot_run 5 / broken 0 of 21 measured.
# 🔴 THIRTEEN COMMITS LANDED BETWEEN v1.0.51 AND THIS CUT. ONLY TWO OF THEM
# REACH THE DMG, AND THIS BOM HAS TWO ROWS BECAUSE OF IT, NOT BECAUSE THE
# OTHER ELEVEN WERE FORGOTTEN.
# A BOM is a claim about what the ARTEFACT CONTAINS. The v1.0.51 BOM already
# established the discipline and the measurement: CM051 #1268 was real work on
# main and was deliberately NOT a row, because `grep -c box_walk_probes
# gui/Makefile` returns 0 against a control (`install.sh`) returning 29 on the
# same file. I RE-RAN THAT EXACT CHECK ON TODAY'S main (cef9c20c) RATHER THAN
# CARRYING THE CLAIM FORWARD: box_walk_probes 0, install.sh 29. The zero is
# real absence and the predicate demonstrably reads that file.
# MEASURED, per commit, over v1.0.51^{commit}..cef9c20c -- files matching
# ^(install\.sh|install\.sh\.strings|gui/|vendor/|assistant-agent/):
#     ac4aad4f  ship=0   cut: third mount leak
#     1b518be3  ship=0   docs(rollforward): disposition the cannot_run bucket
#     6ba237b5  ship=0   fix(walk): CANNOT-RUN must name its prerequisite
#     fae8746e  ship=0   fix(walk): record states how many probes MEASURED
#     cce32b41  ship=2   fix(install): warn before the 3.5GB vane pull    <-- ROW 1
#     ea724af7  ship=0   fix(probe): -K path single-quoted
#     63943390  ship=0   fix(probe): transport failure is CANNOT-RUN everywhere
#     935a1305  ship=0   fix(probe): $HOME expanded on the CONTROLLER
#     cf5dcad9  ship=0   docs(probe): mention count 23 -> 5
#     e5d83b1c  ship=0   walk(record): v1.0.51 record
#     fd31ef8d  ship=0   fix(probe): four keyless store probes present -K
#     19fd3931  ship=1   fix(install): secrets DIRECTORY needs 0700       <-- ROW 2
#     cef9c20c  ship=0   fix(rollforward): walk closure RED on two counts
#     CONTROL: install.sh touches across the whole range = 2, so the
#     ship-predicate is not uniformly zero and can distinguish the two.
# ⇒ ELEVEN of thirteen are probe, CI, walk-record and registry work. They are
# real and they are merged; they are not IN THE DMG. Writing them as rows
# would claim the artefact contains them, and every one would sit permanently
# at landed=no because no walk can ever find them there. That is the #1268
# lesson applied rather than quoted.
# 🟠 BOTH ROWS ARE capability_id=none, AND THAT IS A REAL GAP, NOT A FORMALITY
# manifest/capability_manifest.tsv declares 84 capability ids (control: the
# v1.0.51 row id `install_cm052_pip_stage_outside_bundle` resolves, so the
# lookup works). NEITHER shipping change has one. Both rows are therefore
# UNGUARDED: nothing in gates/capability_matrix.sh can prove them present in
# the artefact, and either can silently regress.
# I did NOT invent capability ids for changes I did not write. @ARCHIE owns
# both fixes and should name them; bom_add.sh explicitly calls "naming a
# capability whose manifest row lands in the same change" a legitimate order
# of work. Flagged here rather than papered over, because a row that reads
# GUARDED while nothing checks it is worse than one honestly marked none.

🟠 THE 3.5 GB VANE PULL WENT SILENT, AND THE COMMENT ABOVE IT SAID IT DID NOT. install.sh pulls the vane image with no progress surface, so a customer on a slow link sees an installer that has apparently stopped for several minutes during the single largest download of the install. The in-file comment asserted the opposite -- that the step already warned -- which is the documentation-not-behaviour class: the comment was the only thing anyone had checked. FIX (#1283): warn before the pull, and correct the comment so the file no longer states something false about itself. Ships because it is install.sh plus its en-GB strings, the two files in this range that reach the artefact.

🔴 THE SECRETS DIRECTORY WAS NOT 0700, AND THE OBVIOUS ONE-LINER WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT. The store credential file is written 0600 owner-only (umask 0077 before the truncate), but the DIRECTORY holding it took the ambient umask -- so the file was protected and its container was not. `mkdir -p -m 700` would not have closed it either, because -m applies only when mkdir actually creates the directory and is a no-op on a pre-existing one, which is exactly the upgrade case. FIX (#1289): set the mode explicitly rather than relying on creation-time flags. Directly adjacent to #549/#550, the multi-account store-exposure lane: a 0600 file inside a 0755 directory still leaks its existence and its metadata to every local account.
